questions.question: How many countries share the natural heritage of the Caspian Sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caspian Sea **

 
 
• The **Caspian Sea**, which is frequently referred to as the** largest lake **or **a true sea,** is the** largest inland body of water in the entire planet**.
 
• An **endorheic basin**, it is located between **Europe and Asia**, which is bordered by the **Caucasus Mountains** to the east,** the Iranian Plateau** to the north, the rich plains of **Southern Russia **to the south, and the wide** steppe of Central Asia to the west**.
 
• With the exception of the extremely salty lagoon of **Garabogazköl **to the east, it has a surface area of 1**43,550 sq mi (372,000 km²)** and a** volume of 78,200 km³**.
 
• The natural heritage of Caspian sea are shared **by five countries** including, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Turkmenistan.
 
• **Kazakhstan **to the northeast**, Russia** to the northwest,** Azerbaijan **to the southwest,** Iran **to the south, and** Turkmenistan **to the southeast form the borders of the Caspian Sea.
 
• The Caspian Sea is famous for its** caviar and oil industries and is home to a variety of species**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://ifpnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/89857-004-0D011EC4.gif] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Like the Black Sea, the **Caspian Sea** is a remnant of the former** Paratethys Sea**.
 
• **Other names of Caspian Sea**
 
 
• The lake is known as the **Mazandaran Sea in Iran**, named for the **famous Mazandaran Province** that sits on its southern banks.
 
• In early **Russian sources** it is mentioned as **The Khvalyn or Khvalis Sea** (after the name of Khwarezmia).
 
• In classical antiquity, it was the **Hyrcanian ocean among the Greeks and Persians**.
 
• The **Abbacuch Sea, Mar de Bachu,** or **Mar de Sala** were the names given to it on **maps made in the Renaissance Europe**.
 
 
 
• In order to further c**onserve the Caspian Sea's biodiversity, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev** signed the Protocol for the Protection of the **Caspian Sea against Pollution from Land-based Sources on October 23, 2021**.

questions.question: Who among the following described the Indian Constitution as ‘quasi federal’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KC Wheare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quasi Federalism**

 
 
• A state that exists somewhere between **a unitary state** and** a federation **is said to practise **quasi-federalism**.
 
• It incorporates the** **positive aspects of both **a federal and a unitary government**.
 
• According to** Prof. K.C. Wheare, India is viewed as** a semi-federal state or a **quasi-federal state**.
 
• It is also described as a **federal system **with a strong bias in favour of the Centre **by the Supreme Court of India**.
 
• The Indian Constitution establishes a federal system of government since it has all the typical characteristics of a federation, including **bicameralism, independent judiciary, dual administration, and the division of powers. It is also written, supreme, and rigorous**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• According to Article 1 of the Indian Constitution, "India, which is Bharat, must be a union of states."
 
• The Indian Constitution is both **federal in design and unitary in spirit**, making it quasi-federal in nature.
 
• **The** **unitary features of the Indian constitution are:**__
 
 
• Single Constitution
 
• Rajya Sabha does not represent the States equality
 
• Division of power is not equal
 
• Existence of States depends on the Centre
 
• Constitution is not strictly rigid
 
• Unified judiciary
 
• ​Proclamation of emergency

questions.question: To combat inflation, what is the usual monetary policy stance adopted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Hawkish__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hawkish monetary policy**

 
 
• An** inflation Hawk or a Hawk **is a financial expert or policymaker who thinks that high interest rates should be maintained in monetary policies to control inflation.
 
• **High interest rates** are primarily of importance to them in **relation to fiscal policy**.
 
• Although they generally support an economy that is running below its** full-employment equilibrium, hawks are not very concerned with economic growth**.
 
• In other words, **Hawks** see high interest rates as a check on **inflation and inflation as their top priority**.
 
• People looking for work may find it difficult while** hawks are in charge because employment doesn't usually rise as quickly**. 
 
• However, hawkish policies are advantageous for those **on fixed incomes since they prevent their dollars' purchasing** value from declining, as it would in a **situation of inflation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Owlish**

 
 
• **Markets and business after three years of James Bond-like** comments from a governor recognised for many memorable phrases, people are now anticipating the** "owlish" monetary policy**.
 
 
 
• **Dovish**
 
 
• **Dove** is a term for an **economist** who supports **monetary policies with low interest rates**.
 
• According to the doves, inflation is not always harmful and won't have a significant** negative impact on the economy**.
 
• They also think that **maintaining low interest rates through monetary policy** benefits a country's overall economy.
 
 
 
• **Hicksian **
 
 
• **Hicks** insisted repeatedly that the **monetary theory had passed into history**.
 
• He was** trying to convey the idea that economic theory **is intrinsically linked to actual occurrences, and more crucially, that monetary concerns must be examined within** a dynamic sequential framework** in which time is a crucial factor.

questions.question: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Translate the mRNA into proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes of a Polysome **

 
 
• The **cellular organelles** known as** ribosomes** are made up of **proteins and rRNA**.
 
• Before they bind to mRNA, they are **present free in the cytoplasm**.
 
• Multiple ribosomes that are joined to the** mRNA **and contain developing **polypeptide chains** are known as** polysomes**.
 
• A **polysome** is made up of** **all the ribosomes that translate a **single mRNA into many polypeptides (Proteins)** at once.
 
• The **coding portion of mRNA**, which is transported by **multiple **ribosomes, forms a **polysome**.
 
• The presence of** so much mRNA in cells **is due to the **ability of multiple ribosomes** to participate in an **mRNA's function**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic, eukaryotic, and membrane-bound polrsomes** all have different structures of multiple ribosomes also known as **polyribosomes**.
 
• **Bacterial polysomes** are found in** double-row formations in prokaryotic cells**, and ribosomes are in touch with one another within smaller subunits.
 
• Planar double row** polysomes and densely packed 3D helices**, which are similar to that of prokaryotic polysomes, are also present in** eukaryotic cells**.
 
• **Polysomal profiling** is a method for** **determining the level of gene expression by monitoring polysome activity. 
 
• Translation is stopped using polysomal profiling, and **sucrose gradient **is then used to separate the resultant cells so that they may be collected by centrifugation.

• Acetic acid was first made or created from **inorganic components in 1845 by German scientist Hermann Kolbe**.
 
• He created **carbon disulfide with chlorine,** and the end result was** carbon tetrachloride**.
 
• After that, **tetrachloroethylene **was produced through** thermal decomposition, trichloroacetic acid **was created through **aqueous chlorination, and acetic acid** was finally produced through an** electrolytic reduction**.
 
• He exclusively used inorganic materials made of** hydrocarbons**.
 
• **Carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen** are inorganic elements that are used to create** acetic acid** while **acetic acid** is an **organic one**.
 
• Acetic acid has a chemical formula and is a **weak acid**.
 
• **Kolbe's work** was groundbreaking since he **synthesised organic chemicals from inorganic ones**.
 
• In addition to **bacterial fermentation, acetic acid is also made synthetically**.
 
• **Some fruits** naturally contain it.

questions.question: Identify the factor that does NOT affect the salinity of the ocean.

options.text: The type of marine organisms found in the water bodies
The rate of evaporation and precipitation
The amount of fresh water flowing into the ocean

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**T**____**he type of marine organisms found in the water bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salinity of the Seawater **
 
• By dividing the weight of the** dissolved substances **by the weight of the** seawater sample,** salinity of seawater is calculated.
 
• The** weight of a kilogram of seawater** is determined by the **fraction per thousand of solid matter** (present as dissolved solid matter) that it contains.
 
• Following are some of the **factors **that effect saltwater salinity:
 
 
• **Evaporation and precipitation** play a major role in **determining the salinity of the water** in the ocean's surface layer.
 
• River freshwater flow has a significant impact on surface **salinity in coastal areas**, and ice freezing and thawing processes have an impact in polar regions.
 
• **Wind** also affects the seawater salinity by **moving water to nearby locations**.
 
• The fluctuations in salinity are caused by **ocean currents**.
 
• **Water density, temperature, and salinity** are all connected. As a result, any **change in temperature or density affects the salinity of water** in an area.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Factors**
 **Affect on Seawater Salinity**
 
 

 Rate of evaporation and precipitation
 Water molecules are removed during evaporation from the water's surface, leaving behind salt and increases the salinity.
 
 

 Amount of fresh water flowing into the ocean
 River freshwater tends to lower ocean salinity.
 
 

 Wind
 High wind stress causes more evaporation, which increases the amount of salt in the seawater.

questions.question: The systematic name of which compound is nitrogen trihydride that is widely used in many industrial processes, and as a fertiliser and refrigerant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ammonia.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ammonia** is used in many industrial processes, and as a fertilizer and refrigerant.
 
• **Ammonia** is a colorless, pungent, suffocating, highly water-soluble, gaseous compound, usually produced by the direct combination of nitrogen and hydrogen.
 
• It is used chiefly for **refrigeration**, and in the manufacturing of chemicals.
 
• Ammonia is a compound with the molecular formula of** NH3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Potash**__ is used **primarily in fertilizers (approximately 95%)** to support plant growth**, ****increase crop yield and disease resistance, and enhance water preservation.**
 
• __**Urea**__ has important uses as a **fertilizer and feed supplement,** as well as a starting material for the manufacture of** plastics and drugs**.
 
• It is a colorless, crystalline substance that melts at 132.7° C (271° F) and decomposes before boiling.
 
• __**Phosphine**__ is **used in the semiconductor industry to introduce phosphorus into silicon crystals** . 
 
• It is also used as a** fumigant, a polymerization initiator** and as an intermediate for the preparation of several flame retardants.

questions.question: Rama Vaidyanathan was awarded with the honour of the Devadasi National Award in 2013 for her contribution in which of the following Indian dance forms?

questions.question: In which sport is the term LONA used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Kabaddi.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Kabaddi**, a team scores a bonus of two points, called a "**lona**", if the entire opposing team is declared out.
 
• **A bonus scored in the game of kabaddi for getting the entire opposing team declared as out**.
 
• If a team can eliminate all seven players of the opposition team, they earn **two extra points** via all out or Lona
 
• After a team scores a Lona, all members of the opposition team are revived and play resumes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kho Kho

 
 
• **Kho Kho** is a traditional Indian sport, being one of the oldest outdoor sports dating back to ancient India. 
 
• It is the second most popular traditional tag game in the Indian subcontinent after Kabaddi.
 
 
 
• Volleyball 
 
 
• **Volleyball** is a team sport in which two teams of six players are separated by a net. 
 
• Each team tries to score points by grounding a ball on the other team's court under organized rules. 
 
• It has been a part of the official program of the **S****u**mmer Olympic Games since Tokyo 1964.
 
 
 
• Softball
 
 
• **Softball **is played by **two teams of 9 players each who try to score more runs than their opponent by rounding the bases and crossing home plate as many times as possible**. 
 
• The batting team stays up to bat until the fielding team puts out 3 batters.
